text: To the angel in Sardis: he who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars says he knows their works; they have a reputation for being alive but are dead.
Wake up and strengthen what remains, which is about to die, for he has not found their works complete before his God.
So remember what they received and heard, keep it, and repent; if they do not wake up he will come like a thief at an hour they will not know.
Yet a few in Sardis have not soiled their clothes, and they will walk with him in white, for they are worthy.
The conqueror will be dressed in white, his name will not be blotted out of the book of life, and he will be acknowledged before the Father and the angels.
Whoever has an ear should hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
To the angel in Philadelphia: the holy and true one, who holds David's key and opens what no one can shut and shuts what no one can open, says this.
He knows their works and has set before them an open door that no one can shut; they have little strength, yet kept his word and did not deny his name.
He will make those of the synagogue of Satan, who falsely claim to be Jews, come and bow at their feet and know that he has loved them.
Because they kept his word of endurance, he will keep them from the hour of trial coming on the whole world to test the earth's inhabitants.
He is coming soon; they should hold fast so no one takes their crown.
The conqueror he will make a pillar in the temple of his God, never to leave it, and he will write on that person the name of his God, the name of the new Jerusalem, and his own new name.
Whoever has an ear should hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
To the angel in Laodicea: the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of God's creation, says this.
He knows their works: they are neither cold nor hot. He wishes they were one or the other.
Because they are lukewarm, neither hot nor cold, he is about to spit them out of his mouth.
They say they are rich and need nothing, not knowing they are wretched, pitiful, poor, blind and naked.
He counsels them to buy from him gold refined by fire to be rich, white garments to cover their shame, and salve to anoint their eyes so they can see.
Those he loves he corrects and disciplines, so they should be earnest and repent.
Look, he stands at the door and knocks; if anyone hears his voice and opens, he will come in and eat with them, and they with him.
The conqueror he will seat with him on his throne, as he conquered and sat with his Father on his throne.
Whoever has an ear should hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
